description: Confronting Shoreline Erosion on O‘ahu is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by University of Hawaiʻi Sea Grant | Center for Coastal and Climate Science and Resilience; State of Hawai‘i Climate Adaptation Initiative; State of Hawai‘i | Department of Land and Natural Resources | Office of Conservation and Coastal Lands. Each winter, massive waves attract surfers and visitors to the North Shore of O‘ahu in Hawai‘i. Some years, the waves cause severe erosion, and continuing sea level rise will accelerate this issue. Residents and the state are taking steps to preserve homes and beaches. Coverage: the United States (2016). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
